p1.s-prophecy--the-mongols-and-the-fall-.text: Checked against the open hadith dataset on 7 October 2026. Bukhari 2928 names the Turks; Bukhari 3590 is a different report (Khuz and Kirman); Abu Dawud 4306 names a city called al-Basrah, not Baghdad. Linking it to the Mongol conquest of 1258 is an interpretation, not stated in the text. A corrected entry is drafted in the review desk. The Sa'id ibn Jumhan death date, the Ibn Taymiyya quote and the 'Basra Gate' are not verified. Recommendation: use with care.

p1.s-hadith--hadith-were-written-down-in.text: Checked on 8 October 2026. Verified in the open hadith dataset: Bukhari 113, Bukhari 2434 ('Write it for Abu Shah'), Abu Dawud 3646 (sahih per al-Albani, al-Muhyi and Zubair Ali Zai), Muslim 3004 and Muslim 1370 (Ali's sheet). Not confirmed from available sources: the counts '138 hadith' and 'ninety-eight in Bukhari or Muslim', and the claim that the whole sahifa is in Musnad Ahmad (one source says all but two hadith). Hammam ibn Munabbih's death is dated 101 AH by Hamidullah and 130 AH by Jonathan Brown, so 'mid-first century' is an inference. Cite Speight and Motzki from their own publications before using their wording on screen.

p1.s-prophecy--the-romans-will-be-victor.text: Checked on 8 October 2026. Quran 30:2-4 wording verified. Gibbon's sentence confirmed in chapter 46 on CCEL, where Gibbon reports the prediction as 'said to have been delivered'. Not confirmed from available sources: the battle of 'Issus, 622' as named here, and the library's description of Tesei's paper. Tirmidhi 3194 (the wager) is graded daif by al-Albani and hasan by Shakir, Bashar Awad and Zubair Ali Zai, and Tirmidhi 3193 (the 'extend the term' detail) is daif by al-Albani and sahih or hasan by others, so scholars differ. The text does not say when the three to nine years start, so how well 622 to 627 fits depends on the date of revelation. A safer wording is in overnight/scripts/B2-romans-prophecy.md.
Scholars grade this report differently. Grades: Ahmad Muhammad Shakir: Hasan; Al-Albani: Daif; Bashar Awad Maarouf: Hasan Sahih; Zubair Ali Zai: Isnaad Hasan.

p5.s-hadith-obj--other-hadith-objections.text: Checked on 9 October 2026. The practice answer calls the Buda'ah narrator 'unknown' and the summary calls the Black Stone report 'weak', but this card's own evidence, and every grader in the open dataset, grade both reports sahih or hasan (Abu Dawud 67; Tirmidhi 959). Do not say either report is weak; explain them instead, as the evidence row does.
